A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated that GluR1 is a key subunit in the expression of L‐type synaptic plasticity in ACC neurons and may play important roles in the regulation of ACC functions.

GluR1‐containing AMPARs are essential for the expression of cingulate L‐type synaptic potentiation, and that the Glu‐R1 recruitment is rapid and completed within the first 5–10min after LTP induction, and that the recruitment is mediated by a postsynaptic mechanism.
we have demonstrated a rapid and time‐dependent GluR1 recruitment in the ACC LTP, and such GluR1‐dependent LTP in the cingulated neurons is critical for learning and memory.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the AMPA receptor subunit GluR1 is essential for synaptic potentiation in the cingulated cortex.
the Glu1 receptor is essential for synaptic potentiation and memory formation.
the AMPA receptor subunit GluR1 plays an important role in the cingulated synaptic plasticity.
